about: READ-ONLY: renders what `delete-forgejo-premove-copy` WOULD delete, and changes nothing (infra/forge/move-forgejo-data.sh --plan-delete; backlog 192a9003). It takes no param: the path is derived, never named — /opt/forgejo/data.pre-move-<first 8 hex of the UUID of the drive the live bind is on>, the rename target move-forgejo-data derives the same way, or that path's deleting- twin when a delete was stopped part-way. Every precondition the write evaluates is evaluated here, and any that fails is a refusal, exit 78, not a plan: Forgejo runs and its /api/healthz passes; the container's /data is the moved copy <boss-data mount>/forgejo-data by device and inode and is not the copy to delete; the repository it serves is the moved copy's; the registry serves the manifest of the converge's current stamp (the rollback target the registry prune always keeps); /opt/forgejo/data is mounted as the move's bind and /etc/fstab carries exactly the move's bind line and the drive's own by-UUID line; the served marker the move left is the record a move writes and is at least 24 hours old (the rollback window); no move-forgejo-data or roll-back-forgejo-data-move run still holds the converge; exactly one copy matches, a real directory on the root filesystem, not a mount, nothing mounted beneath it, mounted by no running container and held by no host process. The plan names the act as the argv the write executes (the rename, then rm -rf --one-file-system), the copy's exact allocated bytes, entry count and top-level entries (nothing writes it, so an exact count is stable), the moved copy and its fstab lines, the marker's record, when the move went live and from when a delete is allowed, and the free-space growth the write must prove. No clock in the bytes; its sha256 is printed on stderr as `plan-sha256:`, and that hash is what David's passkey signs (design 17835005 q1).
